recommendations.body: `_render_committed_step()` in `plan_tool/jira_handoff.py` (step 4 "Define the generated Jira developer-handoff format and lifecycle") never renders `committed_input.file_excerpts` for a `done` step — only the non-`is_done` branch calls `_render_file_excerpts()`. `plan_tool/jira.py:capture_companion_export_input` (`_capture_step_file_excerpts`) unconditionally captures excerpts for every committed step including `done` ones, so the data reaches `HandoffRenderInput` and is then silently discarded for done steps. The plan's Architecture section states a done step's "selected detail and excerpt can provide historical context," but only selected detail actually renders — a developer reading the historical section for a completed step with declared files never sees its captured excerpt, even though it was captured specifically to be available. No test in `tests/test_jira_handoff.py` exercises `file_excerpts` on a done step, so nothing pins this omission as deliberate.
recommendations.suggested_action: in the `is_done` branch of `_render_committed_step()`, also emit `_render_file_excerpts(committed_input.file_excerpts)` under a "Declared files" (or similarly labeled historical) heading when excerpts are present, alongside the existing selected-detail historical block.

recommendations.body: `compute_input_fingerprint()` in `plan_tool/jira_handoff.py` never includes the resolved epic, plan tag, max-hours, or first story number (`plan_tool/jira.py:_CompanionExportSettings.epic/.plan_tag/.max_hours/.start_number`) in its SHA-256 payload, and `HandoffRenderInput` carries no field for them — unlike `format`, which flows in via `pair_identity.format`, and the two contract revisions, which are written as literal `CompanionProvenance` fields even though also outside the hash. The plan's Testing section states that mutating "epic, tag, format, max-hours, or first story number changes both regenerated source files on the next companion-mode invocation," but the handoff body never references these settings and no part of its embedded `CompanionProvenance` block reflects them, so the handoff file's bytes are fully invariant to an epic/plan-tag/max-hours/story-number-only change — contradicting that Testing-section claim for the handoff side of the pair.
recommendations.suggested_action: add fields for the resolved epic, plan tag, max-hours, and first story number to `HandoffRenderInput` (or thread them into `compute_input_fingerprint()`/`build_companion_provenance()` as an explicit settings parameter) and fold them into the fingerprint payload dict.
